target.title: feat(browser): send pages to OpenClaw from the Chrome extension
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

There was no way to hand the page you are looking at to your OpenClaw agent. The community tool [Nateliason/send-to-openclaw](https://github.com/Nateliason/send-to-openclaw) proved the demand, but it needs a separate Chrome extension plus a local Express webhook server that shells out to the CLI — an entire second install and token surface that exists only because a vanilla extension has no authenticated path to the Gateway. Our extension already owns one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fold "send this page to my agent" into the official OpenClaw Chrome extension as a third feature next to tab control and the tab copilot, riding the existing paired relay WebSocket:

- **Extension**: toolbar-popup send button with an optional note, a page/selection context-menu item, and an `Alt+Shift+S` command. Capture is selection-first, with a readability-style heuristic, X/Twitter thread extraction, and Google Docs plain-text export fetched inside the tab so the user's cookies apply (no Google API setup). New `pageShare` extension→relay message with correlated `pageShareResult` acks.
- **Gateway**: the relay bridge validates payloads (size caps included) and hands them to a page-share sink registered only by the browser plugin's Gateway service — plugin services never start on node hosts, so node-hosted relays return a clear "not supported" error instead of black-holing events in a process with no agent loop. Delivery matches `POST /hooks/wake` semantics exactly: system event on the main session + immediate heartbeat.
- **Safety**: page text is wrapped with `wrapExternalContent(source: "browser")`; the user's typed note stays outside the wrapper as their own instruction. System-tag sanitization applies at the queue boundary as usual.
- **SDK**: one additive export (`resolveMainSessionKeyFromConfig` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/system-event-runtime`) with the surface budget bumped +1/+1 and the ledger comment updated.

Capture heuristics adapted from Nat Eliason's MIT-licensed send-to-openclaw (credit: @Nateliason).

## User Impact

Pair the extension once, then send any page, Google Doc, X thread, or text selection to your main session in one click/keystroke — no extra server, port, token, or config. The tab does not need to be in the OpenClaw tab group; a share is one-shot and grants no ongoing access. Docs: new "Send a page to OpenClaw" section in `docs/tools/chrome-extension.md`.

## Evidence

- Focused suites (local, worktree lock scope): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/ extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/page-share-core.test.ts extensions/browser/src/plugin-service.test.ts extensions/browser/chrome-extension/background.test.ts` → **9 files, 54 tests passed**.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (8158 exports / 4540 callable, +1/+1 documented).
- Live end-to-end proof against a scratch Gateway (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, port 19477): real Chromium + unpacked extension paired over the direct Gateway route (`[browser/extension-relay-gateway] extension connected over gateway for profile "chrome"`), sent https://example.com with a note → extension received `{"ok":true}`, which the bridge only sends after `deliverPageShare` resolved (system event enqueued + immediate heartbeat requested in the Gateway process). Driver used a scoped test `host_permissions` copy because scripted messages are not user gestures; real popup/menu/shortcut clicks are gestures, so the shipped manifest needs only `activeTab`.
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): three review cycles, all findings fixed — (1) page-controlled title/URL moved inside the untrusted-content boundary, (2) selection-first enforced for Google Docs instead of always exporting the full document, (3) context-menu shares rebuilt as click-time snapshots (no recapture) so navigation races and iframe selections cannot mislabel or lose content, (4) the Docs selection probe reduced to a deterministic main-frame read with the child-frame tradeoff named in a code comment. Final run: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings`, "patch is correct (0.96)".
- Scanner note: the helper's secret scan rejects any diff touching the pre-existing `ROTATED_TOKEN = "b".repeat(64)` fixture in `relay-lifecycle.test.ts`, so that file's one-line assertion update (`onPageShare: expect.any(Function)`) landed as its own commit outside the helper bundle and was reviewed by hand.
